title: The sigmoid function
hints: For very negative x, e^(−x) is enormous. Python's math.exp raises OverflowError past about 709; Rust and C++ return infinity, which happens to work.
A stable version: if x ≥ 0 use 1 / (1 + e^(−x)); otherwise use e^x / (1 + e^x). Both are the same function, but neither ever computes a huge exponential.

tests.description: positive inputs give values above ½
negative inputs give values below ½
very negative inputs give 0 (watch out for overflow!)
